**[VELTRIS CONSUMER BRANDS, INC.]{.underline}**

**[BRAND GOVERNANCE COMMITTEE CHARTER]{.underline}**

**Adopted by the Board of Directors** **Effective April 12, 2024**

Right-click to update Table of Contents

**[Article I --- Purpose]{.underline}**

The Brand Governance Committee (the \"BGC\" or the \"Committee\") is established by the Board of Directors of Veltris Consumer Brands, Inc. (\"Veltris\" or the \"Company\") for the purpose of providing centralized oversight, strategic direction, and approval authority over the use, licensing, and protection of the Company\'s brand assets, trademarks, trade dress, and associated intellectual property. The Committee serves as the principal governance body charged with ensuring that the Company\'s brand portfolio is managed in a manner consistent with the Company\'s long-term brand strategy, financial objectives, and legal obligations.

The Committee is designated as the escalation body under the Veltris IP Licensing Policy, Rev. 4.0 (effective April 12, 2024) (the \"IP Licensing Policy\"), and is responsible for reviewing and adjudicating IP licensing transactions that exceed the delegated authority thresholds established therein. In this capacity, the Committee evaluates proposed deviations from the Company\'s standard licensing terms, assesses the financial and reputational implications of such deviations, and renders binding determinations regarding the acceptability of non-standard terms in license agreements involving the Company\'s intellectual property.

The Committee exercises its authority on behalf of the Board of Directors. The Committee shall report to the Board on a quarterly basis, providing a comprehensive summary of escalation activity, disposition of reviewed matters, material developments in the IP licensing landscape, and any recommended amendments to the IP Licensing Policy or related governance instruments. The Committee\'s authority is subject to the limitations set forth in this Charter and to the ultimate oversight of the Board.

Nothing in this Charter shall be construed to diminish or supersede the authority of the Board of Directors to take direct action on any matter within the Committee\'s jurisdiction. The Board retains full authority to review, modify, or reverse any action taken by the Committee.

**[Article II --- Definitions]{.underline}**

The following defined terms shall have the meanings set forth below when used throughout this Charter. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Article II shall have the meanings ascribed to them elsewhere in this Charter or, if not defined herein, in the IP Licensing Policy.

**\"Board\"** means the Board of Directors of Veltris Consumer Brands, Inc.

**\"Chair\"** means the chairperson of the Brand Governance Committee, as designated in Article III, Section 3.1 of this Charter.

**\"Committee\"** or **\"BGC\"** means the Brand Governance Committee established by this Charter.

**\"Company\"** means Veltris Consumer Brands, Inc., a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware.

**\"Escalation Memo\"** means a written memorandum submitted to the Committee pursuant to Article VI of this Charter requesting review or approval of an out-of-policy IP licensing matter. The required form and content of an Escalation Memo are set forth in Article VI, Section 6.1, and the standard form template is attached hereto as Annex B.

**\"IP Licensing Policy\"** means the Veltris IP Licensing Policy, Rev. 4.0, effective April 12, 2024, as amended from time to time, including all sections referenced therein (§§ 5.1--5.8, § 6, and any successor provisions).

**\"Licensed IP\"** means any trademark, service mark, trade name, trade dress, logo, design mark, color mark, tagline, or other intellectual property asset owned or controlled by Veltris, whether registered or unregistered, domestic or international, including all goodwill associated therewith.

**\"Member\"** means a standing or ex officio member of the Committee as set forth in Article III of this Charter.

**\"Special Session\"** means a Committee meeting convened outside the regular meeting schedule pursuant to Article V, Section 5.3 of this Charter.

**[Article III --- Composition and Membership]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Chair**

The Committee shall be chaired by the Senior Vice President --- Brand Strategy of the Company. As of the effective date of this Charter, the Chair is **Erik Lindgren, SVP -- Brand Strategy**. The Chair shall preside over all meetings of the Committee, establish and circulate meeting agendas, and serve as the Committee\'s primary liaison to the Board of Directors and the Chief Legal Officer. In the event of the Chair\'s absence, incapacity, or recusal from a particular matter, the Chair shall designate an acting chair from among the standing members to preside over the relevant meeting or portion thereof. If the Chair has not designated an acting chair, the most senior standing member from the Legal division (by tenure on the Committee) shall serve as acting chair for the duration of the Chair\'s absence.

The Chair shall be responsible for the orderly conduct of Committee meetings, including the management of deliberations, the calling of votes, and the timely distribution of meeting materials. The Chair shall also be responsible for coordinating with the Chief Legal Officer\'s office on all matters involving external legal advisors and for ensuring that Committee resolutions are promptly communicated to the relevant officers and employees of the Company.

**Section 3.2 --- Standing Members**

The Committee shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than seven (7) standing members, drawn from the following functional areas to ensure cross-functional oversight of the Company\'s brand and intellectual property matters:

**Brand Strategy / Marketing.** The Chair (SVP -- Brand Strategy) shall serve as one standing member from this functional area. In addition, one additional senior representative from the Marketing division, at the rank of Vice President or above, shall serve as a standing member. The inclusion of marketing representation ensures that the Committee\'s deliberations are informed by current market positioning, consumer insights, and brand architecture considerations.

**Finance.** Two representatives from the Finance division shall serve as standing members, including (i) a designee of the Chief Financial Officer and (ii) a representative from the Financial Planning & Analysis group. Each Finance representative shall hold the rank of Senior Director or above. The presence of Finance representation ensures that the Committee has direct access to quantitative financial analysis, revenue modeling, and budgetary considerations in evaluating proposed licensing deviations.

**Legal.** Two representatives from the Legal division shall serve as standing members, including (i) a designee of the Chief Legal Officer and (ii) a representative from the IP Licensing group. Each Legal representative shall hold the rank of Senior Counsel or above. Legal representation ensures that the Committee\'s decisions are informed by an understanding of the Company\'s trademark enforcement posture, regulatory compliance obligations, contractual risk allocation, and applicable intellectual property law.

The Chair shall present a slate of proposed standing members to the Board annually for confirmation, in conjunction with the Board\'s first regular meeting of each fiscal year. Standing members serve one-year terms, which are renewable without limitation. A standing member\'s term shall continue until such member\'s successor has been confirmed by the Board, unless the member is removed or resigns pursuant to Section 3.4 below.

**Section 3.3 --- Ex Officio Members**

The following officers of the Company shall serve as non-voting, ex officio members of the Committee and shall receive all Committee materials, notices, and minutes on the same basis as standing members:

> • **Chief Legal Officer** (currently Margaret Solano)
>
> • **Chief Financial Officer** (currently Thomas Kessler)

Ex officio members may attend any meeting of the Committee, whether regular or special, and may participate fully in discussions and deliberations. Ex officio members do not, however, count toward quorum under Article V, Section 5.5 and do not hold voting rights under this Charter unless such officer is separately designated as a standing member in accordance with Section 3.2 above. The purpose of ex officio membership is to ensure that the Company\'s senior executive leadership maintains full visibility into the Committee\'s activities and has the opportunity to provide input on matters within the Committee\'s jurisdiction, particularly where officer-level co-approval is required under the IP Licensing Policy.

**Section 3.4 --- Removal and Vacancy**

The Chair may recommend the replacement of any standing member upon written notice to the Board, specifying the reasons for the proposed replacement. The Board may act on such recommendation at its next regular meeting or by unanimous written consent. A standing member may also resign from the Committee by delivering written notice to the Chair, with a copy to the Chief Legal Officer.

Vacancies on the Committee, whether resulting from removal, resignation, expiration of term without renewal, or any other cause, shall be filled within thirty (30) days by appointment of the Chair, subject to Board ratification at the Board\'s next regular meeting. During any period in which a vacancy exists, quorum calculations under Article V, Section 5.5 shall be based on the number of seated standing members at the time of the meeting, rather than on the maximum number of standing members authorized under Section 3.2. In no event shall the Committee conduct business with fewer than three (3) seated standing members.

**[Article IV --- Authority and Scope]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- General Authority**

The Committee shall have the authority to review, approve, conditionally approve, reject, or remand any matter falling within its jurisdiction as defined in this Article IV and the IP Licensing Policy. The Committee\'s authority extends to all stages of the licensing negotiation process, from preliminary term sheet review through final execution approval, to the extent that any element of a proposed transaction triggers escalation under the IP Licensing Policy or is otherwise referred to the Committee by an authorized officer.

The Committee may request any information from Company personnel, including but not limited to financial projections, market analyses, legal memoranda, and third-party advisor reports, that it deems necessary to discharge its responsibilities. All Company personnel shall cooperate fully with the Committee in connection with its review of escalated matters.

**Section 4.2 --- IP Licensing Transaction Approval**

The Committee shall serve as the approval body for IP licensing transactions escalated under the IP Licensing Policy, including without limitation the following categories of out-of-policy terms:

> \(a\) **Term Deviations.** Any proposed license agreement with an initial term exceeding seven (7) years, or containing unilateral (licensee-only) renewal options that could result in aggregate license durations exceeding the Company\'s standard maximum term, as described in IP Licensing Policy § 5.1(a). The Committee shall evaluate whether the proposed term length is justified by the nature of the licensed brand, the licensee\'s capital investment requirements, the competitive landscape, and the adequacy of protective provisions (including performance benchmarks and termination triggers) included in the proposed agreement.
>
> \(b\) **Royalty and MAG Deviations.** Escalations involving royalty rates or minimum annual guarantee (\"MAG\") amounts that fall below policy-floor thresholds established in IP Licensing Policy §§ 5.2(a)--(b). The Committee shall assess the financial impact of below-floor royalty rates and MAG amounts by reference to the quantitative analysis provided in the Escalation Memo, independent benchmarking data, and the Company\'s internal financial models. Sub-floor royalty rates require joint co-approval of the Chief Financial Officer and the Chief Legal Officer in addition to Committee review, as specified in IP Licensing Policy § 5.2(a). The Committee shall not approve a sub-floor royalty rate unless such officer-level co-approvals have been obtained or are conditioned as set forth in Section 4.4 below.
>
> \(c\) **Quality Control and Audit Deviations.** Any proposed modifications to the Company\'s standard audit rights, quality-control inspection provisions, or deemed-approval mechanisms that deviate from the requirements of IP Licensing Policy § 5.3. The Committee recognizes that the Company\'s audit and quality-control rights are essential to the maintenance of trademark rights under the Lanham Act and to the preservation of brand integrity. Accordingly, the Committee shall apply heightened scrutiny to any proposed diminution of these rights and shall require a detailed analysis of the legal and reputational risks associated with any proposed deviation.
>
> \(d\) **Termination Provisions.** Proposed limitations on or elimination of the licensor\'s convenience termination right, extensions of post-termination sell-off periods beyond the twelve (12) months permitted under IP Licensing Policy § 5.5, or modifications to cure periods applicable to licensee defaults. The Committee shall evaluate the impact of any proposed termination-related deviation on the Company\'s ability to protect its brands and to respond to changes in market conditions, licensee performance, or brand strategy.
>
> \(e\) **Sublicensing.** Proposed sublicense rights that deviate from the requirement of prior written Veltris consent for all sublicenses, including blanket sublicensing to controlled affiliates, as addressed in IP Licensing Policy § 5.6. The Committee shall consider the identity, financial condition, and brand management capabilities of potential sublicensees and shall assess the adequacy of flow-down provisions ensuring that sublicensees are bound by the same quality-control, audit, and termination standards applicable to the primary licensee.
>
> \(f\) **Dispute Resolution.** Any proposed departure from the default governing law (North Carolina), forum selection (Mecklenburg County, North Carolina state courts), or agreement to binding arbitration. Proposals involving alternative dispute resolution mechanisms or foreign governing law additionally require the Chief Legal Officer\'s separate approval under IP Licensing Policy § 5.7. The Committee shall evaluate the enforceability, convenience, and strategic implications of any proposed departure from the Company\'s standard dispute resolution provisions.
>
> \(g\) **Indemnification and Liability.** Proposed caps on licensee indemnification obligations or expansions of licensor liability caps beyond the twelve (12)-month trailing royalty standard established in IP Licensing Policy § 5.4. The Committee shall assess the Company\'s exposure under the proposed indemnification and liability framework, taking into account the nature of the licensed products, the licensee\'s insurance coverage, and the Company\'s historical claims experience in the relevant product category.
>
> \(h\) **Other Matters.** Any IP licensing matter referred to the Committee by the Chief Legal Officer, the VP of IP Licensing, or the Board. The Committee shall accept referrals from these sources regardless of whether the matter technically triggers an escalation threshold under the IP Licensing Policy, recognizing that certain matters may present strategic or reputational considerations warranting Committee-level review even in the absence of a specific policy deviation.

**Section 4.3 --- Delegation**

The Committee may not delegate its approval authority under Section 4.2 to any individual officer or employee of the Company. The purpose of this non-delegation principle is to ensure that all out-of-policy licensing decisions receive the benefit of the Committee\'s cross-functional deliberation and collective judgment.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Chair may authorize preliminary conditional terms in the context of ongoing licensing negotiations, subject to full Committee ratification at the next regular or special session. Any preliminary conditional terms authorized by the Chair shall be communicated to the counterparty as expressly subject to Committee approval and shall not create any binding obligation on the Company until such ratification has been obtained.

The VP, IP Licensing (currently Jason Murata) retains delegated authority under the IP Licensing Policy to approve transactions that fall within all policy thresholds established therein. Matters exceeding any threshold must be escalated to the Committee in accordance with Article VI of this Charter. The VP, IP Licensing shall not approve any transaction involving an out-of-policy term without prior Committee authorization, except as may be expressly permitted by a standing resolution of the Committee.

**Section 4.4 --- Coordination with Officer-Level Approvals**

Where the IP Licensing Policy requires approval by the Chief Legal Officer, the Chief Financial Officer, or both, in addition to the Committee, the Committee\'s approval shall not be effective until such officer-level co-approvals have been obtained in writing. The Committee may condition its own approval on the receipt of such co-approvals and may specify a deadline by which such co-approvals must be obtained for the Committee\'s approval to remain effective.

In the event that an officer-level co-approval is denied after the Committee has granted conditional approval, the matter shall be returned to the Committee for further deliberation. The Committee may elect to modify its resolution in light of the officer\'s denial or may refer the matter to the Board of Directors for final determination.

The Chair shall maintain a log of all matters requiring officer-level co-approval and shall track the status of such co-approvals to ensure that no license agreement is executed without all required authorizations having been obtained.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (0-based). Optional.

function.description: Write a plain markdown file (typically `response.md`) to the output directory. For binary deliverables (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx), use the file-type skill manuals — do not write raw markdown to a binary extension. Creates parent directories if needed.
function.name: write

file_path.description: Relative path under the output directory (e.g., 'response.md')

function.description: Perform exact string replacement in a file you have already created or read. The old_string must appear exactly once unless replace_all is true. Use for incremental refinement, not first-time writes.
function.name: edit

file_path.description: Path to the file to modify

old_string.description: The exact text to find and replace

replace_all.description: If true, replace all occurrences. Default false.

function.description: Find files matching a glob pattern, sorted by modification time. Defaults to searching the input directory. Prefer this over `bash find` or `bash ls` for file discovery.
function.name: glob

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the input directory.

function.description: Search file contents using regex patterns. Defaults to searching the input directory. Returns matching file paths or matching lines with context.
function.name: grep

output_mode.description: Output format. 'content' shows matching lines, 'files_with_matches' shows file paths, 'count' shows match counts. Default: 'files_with_matches'.

path.description: File or directory to search in. Defaults to the input directory.
